name: Marla
reason: Roadhouse settlement; Wikivoyage Marla and the Flinders & Outback town page list only fuel, accommodation and Indulkana art centre (a separate place 40+ km away) - nothing to see or do in Marla itself for half an hour (rule 2).

name: Roxby Downs
reason: Mining town; the Flinders & Outback page lists the Roxbylink complex (visitor centre, library, pool) and a 3 km emu trail, i.e. civic facilities and tours. The distinct draw (Arid Recovery) is judged separately; the town itself is a service stop (rule 2).

name: Mungerannie
reason: Mungerannie Hotel is named by Flinders & Outback as acclaimed for its outback memorabilia (hats, locks of hair), a quirky roadside icon halfway along the Birdsville Track; second-tier quirky stop the bar keeps.

name: Lyndhurst
reason: Flinders & Outback town page names Talc Alf's talc sculptures and the ochre cliffs 5 km north (traded by Aboriginal people), plus Farina nearby; a gateway town with things to see, and the Strzelecki Track start per Wikivoyage.

name: Strzelecki Track
reason: A 475 km route, not a place: Wikivoyage describes the drive; its stops (Lyndhurst, Innamincka) are separate candidates. A road/vehicle route is not a spot (rule 3). Objection: Wikivoyage gives it its own article, but nothing to see or do at a single place.

name: Painted Desert (South Australia)
reason: For: Wikivoyage names it, SA Heritage lists the Arckaringa Hills state heritage area, and Arckaringa Station offers a walk (~1.5 km) and lookout at sunset; distinct natural sight. Against: only one counted source (Wikivoyage Stuart Highway, 'all-wheel track'), sits on a private pastoral lease with restricted, fragile access, 120-150 km from Coober Pedy; no tourism-board page found.

name: Tom's Working Opal Mine
reason: Wikivoyage Coober Pedy calls it 'the pick of the working mines' and Lonely Planet lists it as an attraction (display mine with opal seams, guided or self-guided tours); a place to go underground for an hour, not merely an operator. Objection: one of several Coober Pedy mine visits.

name: Catholic Catacomb Church
reason: For: Wikivoyage Coober Pedy calls the underground Catholic church 'a significant site' and Coober Pedy's carved-rock churches are a signature visit. Against: Wikivoyage ranks it less intricate than the Serbian Orthodox church; one counted source; the candidate's wiki title (Catacomb Church) is actually the Anglican church, so name and article conflict and the Catholic church's identity needs checking.

name: Dingo Fence at Coober Pedy
reason: A roadside look at a fence (Wikivoyage Stuart Highway: 10 km on a dirt road; travel blogs say it is passed on the Breakaways road): a short roadside stop with one counted source, not a distinct place for half an hour (rule 3).

name: Coober Pedy Golf Club
reason: Wikivoyage names the grassless desert course (players carry a piece of turf to tee off) as a quirky thing to do 3 km from Coober Pedy; an open public course visitors play, a recognised quirky icon.

name: Moon Plain
reason: Lonely Planet lists Moon Plain and southaustralia.com's region page names the lunar-like plain and film location (Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome, Priscilla) 15 km from Coober Pedy; a driving/walking sight on the Breakaways loop. Two counted sources.

name: Roxby Downs Arid Recovery Reserve
reason: Flinders & Outback names Arid Recovery in both the region page and the Roxby Downs town page (sunset tag-along tours, spotlight walks, Roxby Discovery Tour) to see rare arid-zone species in a fenced reserve; visits are by tour only. Objection: access only via tours.

name: Lake Torrens National Park
reason: Flinders & Outback page only describes a dry salt lake 200 km long; no visitor facilities, viewpoint, walk or access point is named by any source I found, and access is difficult, so there is nothing a visitor is directed to do or see (rule 2). Searched the Flinders & Outback page and web.

name: Marree Man
reason: For: Wikivoyage Marree See entry and Flinders & Outback both name it; a famous 4.2 km geoglyph. Against: it cannot be seen from the ground and the experience is a charter flight from Marree (an operator), so a visitor 'goes' to nothing; only the flight reaches it.

name: Lake Eyre South
reason: Wikivoyage's 3 km side trip shows a salt expanse that is an extension of Lake Eyre, part of Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre National Park, which the app lists; an outlook within a larger spot with one counted source (rule 3).

name: William Creek Hotel
reason: Flinders & Outback and Wikivoyage William Creek both single out the pub (one of the most remote in the world; the town's whole sight, with its own radio station); a quirky outback icon in the same class as Mungerannie. Objection: it is a business and William Creek the town may be listed separately.

name: Innamincka Regional Reserve
reason: parks.sa.gov.au visitor page: 1.3 million ha reserve with Cooper Creek waterholes for fishing and canoeing, Cullyamurra Waterhole, the visitor centre and Burke and Wills sites; Flinders & Outback also names it. Objection: parts closed in floods and it overlaps Cullyamurra.

name: Innamincka Town Sunset Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage Innamincka lists it with only a location (1 km NE of town) and no description; no other counted source; a minor lookout and short stop (rule 3).

name: Lake Harry Ruins and Clayton Station
reason: No counted source names it: Wikivoyage National Route 83, Innamincka and Marree pages and the Flinders & Outback outback page all lack it (grepped). Searched those pages.

name: Cooper Creek Crossing
reason: One counted source (Wikivoyage Innamincka: a causeway where pelicans feed in the evening); a short stop in town, and the creek itself is covered by Innamincka Regional Reserve (rule 3).

name: Mulka Ruins
reason: No counted source names it: Wikivoyage National Route 83 and the Flinders & Outback outback page do not mention Mulka (grepped).

name: Witchelina Nature Reserve
reason: Nature Foundation reserve with no counted source and access limited to members with bookings and fees; not open to the public (rule 2).

name: Kalamurina Sanctuary
reason: For: AWC (the manager) describes a 679,000 ha wildlife sanctuary on the Warburton River with an interpretive walk on Outback Spirit pre-booked tours (April-October). Against: no tourism-board or guide source; third-party listings say camping is closed and entry is tours only, and AWC's own page allows booked self-drive at $40 per vehicle, so access sources conflict.

name: Lake Frome National Park
reason: Wrong region, not this region's: belongs to sa-flinders (reached from Balcanoona); also no counted source found in this pass.

name: Elizabeth Symon Nursing Home
reason: Wikivoyage Innamincka See lists it, and the parks.sa.gov.au page says the heritage-listed park headquarters and interpretation centre (the former Australian Inland Mission building, i.e. the nursing home) is always open in the town centre, with natural history and Burke and Wills displays. Objection: more an information centre than a sight.
